subject: SOC 2 re-attestation: archive policy tweak, bulk evidence transfer & temporary throughput uplift
messages:
From: Elise Morgan <audit@fusebank.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.example>
Cc: Dan Huang <legal@fusebank.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SOC 2 renewal — archive retention carve-out + evidence transfer

Connor / team,

We're kicking off Fuse Bank's annual SOC 2 re-attestation (renewal due 2026-11-01) and wanted to surface a few items that will affect our timeline and a potential capacity increase:

- Retention carve-out: our compliance team needs a temporary adjustment to the log retention window for a 30-day snapshot export (we keep 90 days in prod, we need a 365-day slice for the audit).
- Bulk evidence transfer: we plan to request a bulk transfer of redacted artifacts and log snapshots into our secure evidence escrow ahead of the auditor's first inspection window.
- Throughput: because the snapshot is large (est. 1.2 TB of structured logs + artifacts), we'll need a short burst in transfer throughput and a clear runbook for the transfer to avoid token-throttling on our side.

I've attached an initial evidence index (initial_evidence_index.csv) and a simple timeline. High-level asks: confirmation that Redwood can provide a temporary retention carve-out, a brief runbook for bulk transfer, and whether you can temporarily bump transfer throughput (or provide a burst window) — plus an estimate for any costs/credits for the burst.

Can we get a short call this week to align?

Thanks,
Elise Morgan
Sr. IT Audit Manager
Fuse Bank

Attachment: initial_evidence_index.csv
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.example>
To: Elise Morgan <audit@fusebank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-08-23T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 renewal — archive retention carve-out + evidence transfer

Elise — thanks for the clear summary. We can support the asks; here's a proposed approach to keep scope tight and auditable: 

1) Retention carve-out (short-lived):
   - We will provision a 365-day slice of the required logs as a one-off snapshot (read-only) and preserve it in a compliance carve-out namespace. Retention policy will revert automatically after 45 days unless you request extension.
   - We will provide a manifest and MD5 checksums for every file to support auditor verification.

2) Bulk transfer runbook (attachment):
   - Attached: proposed_transfer_runbook.docx — outlines export steps, secure transfer (S3 presigned + mutually authenticated upload), verification, and rollback.
   - We recommend a canary run on a small shard (5-10 GB) to validate checksums and throughput before committing the full export.

3) Temporary throughput uplift / credits:
   - We can enable a 72-hour burst window with increased egress concurrency and a dedicated transfer lane. Pricing-wise, we can either apply a one-time throughput fee or provide a partial usage credit if this leads into an expansion (seat conversion to reserved capacity). Ben and Kimberly, I've looped you in for pricing & commercial options.

Proposed next steps:
- Internal kickoff: 2026-08-24 10:00 PT (30 min) — I'll send invite.
- Canary export window: 2026-08-26 — small sample transfer.
- Full export target window: 2026-08-28 to 2026-08-30 (72-hour burst).

If that timeline doesn't work, tell us preferred windows. We can also generate the MD5 manifest and invoice estimate ahead of the canary if you need procurement sign-off.

Connor O'Brien
Customer Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_transfer_runbook.docx
From: Dan Huang <legal@fusebank.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.example>, Elise Morgan <audit@fusebank.com>
Date: 2026-08-24T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 renewal — archive retention carve-out + evidence transfer

Connor / Elise — quick legal flag before we proceed: 

- Amendment language: we need to capture the retention carve-out as an addendum (time-limited, explicitly scoped to the artifacts identified in the manifest). Please propose exact wording that limits Redwood's liability beyond the carve-out window.
- Data residency: Fuse Bank is US primary but a small subset of the artifacts contain cross-border metadata. Confirm that the transfer path and escrow location remain in the US and that any subcontractors are bound by the same data residency terms.
- Audit access: auditors will want temporary access to the preserved snapshot. Propose an access model (time-limited signed URL vs. auditor account). We prefer a least-privilege, time-bound signed URL approach.

Once we have wording we can run this past procurement for sign-off.

Thanks,
Dan Huang
Senior Counsel, Compliance
Fuse Bank
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example>
To: Dan Huang <legal@fusebank.com>, Elise Morgan <audit@fusebank.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.example>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-08-24T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 renewal — archive retention carve-out + evidence transfer

Dan / Elise — appreciate the detail. Commercially, we can accommodate the carve-out as a short-term amendment. High level: 

- Suggested amendment snippet (draft): "Redwood will create a time-limited compliance snapshot of artifacts identified in the manifest. Redwood's preservation obligation is limited to the integrity and availability of the snapshot for a period of forty-five (45) days following snapshot completion, unless otherwise extended in writing by the parties."
- Transfer lane pricing: we will absorb 50% of the estimated egress cost if Fuse Bank converts X seats to a 12-month reserved capacity commitment within 30 days of renewal (we can model exact numbers in the attached pricing-sheet-v2.pdf).
- Auditor access model: we support time-limited signed URLs with granular object-level permissions. We will add an audit log of signed URL issuance to the snapshot manifest.

If that language looks acceptable I can produce a short amendment draft (SLA-amendment-draft.docx) and route for signatures. Connor, please confirm the technical runbook details and the canary schedule.

Kimberly Park
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing-sheet-v2.pdf, SLA-amendment-draft.docx
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.example>
To: Elise Morgan <audit@fusebank.com>, Dan Huang <legal@fusebank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-08-25T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 renewal — archive retention carve-out + evidence transfer

Per thread (summary & actions):

- Agreement: Redwood will produce a 365-day snapshot in a compliance namespace, preserve for 45 days by default, and provide MD5 checksums + signed URLs for auditor access.
- Security/residency: All transfer endpoints and escrow storage will be US-based; we will include subcontractor attestations in the amendment.
- Transfer plan: Canary 2026-08-26 (5-10 GB), Full transfer 2026-08-28 to 2026-08-30 (72-hour burst).
- Commercial: Kimberly's team will provide revised pricing and a path to apply a partial credit if Fuse Bank converts to reserved capacity (refer to DEAL-38492).

I've scheduled the 30-min kickoff: 2026-08-24 10:00 PT — calendar invite and the upload Drive folder are here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-fusebank-transfer.

Next immediate asks for Fuse Bank: please confirm acceptance of the draft amendment snippet above and confirm any PII redaction rules the auditor requires before the canary. We'll stand up the canary lane and share the manifest for verification prior to full export.

Connor O'Brien
Customer Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0192
